minutes.headline: Diversity committee's recommendations go to the policy subcommittee; handbook changes reviewed at final meeting of year
minutes.summary: The last meeting of the school year centered on the Committee for Acceptance and Diversity's final report and recommendations, which the chair suggested sending to the policy subcommittee. The committee also reviewed handbook changes on discipline, parking and head lice procedure, and heard superintendent and building project updates. Surplus equipment lists and the summer meeting schedule were also discussed.

attendees.role: presenter, vice chair of the advisory committee for acceptance and diversity

votes.motion: Release executive session minutes from Nov 6, Nov 20, Dec 18 2013 and Feb 26, Mar 5, Mar 19, Apr 2 2014

budget_items.what_was_said: The advisory committee gave a ballpark first-year budget for speakers, materials, training, curriculum and transportation, hoping grants and donations would cover much of it.
The high school principal said the club activity fee is running close to or in the red and may need to increase.
Unrestricted good funds covered two trips; transportation is expensive and the budget carries a minimum for these.
A contractor restored power and a freezer was saved; cost was mentioned.
Surplus equipment would be sold by sealed bid, with limited expected proceeds.

decisions.decision: Chair suggested referring the diversity advisory committee's recommendations to the policy subcommittee to draft language for the regular policy process.
Committee agreed to include the head lice procedure as a building-based procedure referenced in the handbook rather than as policy.
Meeting calendar continues first and third Wednesdays; a July meeting date around the 16th discussed to ensure a quorum.

what_happened.line: The Committee for Acceptance and Diversity gave its final report, and the chair suggested sending its recommendations to the policy subcommittee to draft language.
The advisory committee gave a ballpark first-year budget for speakers, materials, training, curriculum and transportation, hoping grants and donations would cover much of it.
The committee agreed to list the head lice procedure as a building-based procedure referenced in the handbook, not as policy.
The high school principal said the club activity fee is running close to or in the red and may need to increase.
The meeting calendar stays on first and third Wednesdays, with a July date around the 16th discussed to ensure a quorum.

why_it_matters: The diversity recommendations enter the regular policy process, so any cost for training, curriculum or speakers would depend on grants and donations or on a later budget request.
A rising high school activity fee would be paid by families of students in clubs, and no vote on it was taken at this meeting.
watch_next: The policy subcommittee's draft language on the diversity recommendations, and any vote on the activity fee.
A July meeting date around the 16th, which was discussed to ensure a quorum.
